subject: Request: StormTech bespoke uptime & latency commitment
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stormtech.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Chen <victor@stormtech.com>, StormTech Legal <contracts@stormtech.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: Bespoke uptime & latency commitment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's inferencing performance. Before we move to procurement, our platform ops and reliability team have asked for a bespoke commitment for our production inference path: 99.95% monthly uptime and P95 latency under 120ms for the primary low-latency route.

We understand this is outside standard terms; StormTech is evaluating a multi-year committed purchase and this SLA is a gating item. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Offer an exception for this account (dedicated pool or reserved capacity)
- Put a formal uptime and latency commitment in the contract with measurable SLOs and credits
- Share a short runbook for operational escalation and rollback/fallback behavior

If needed, we can arrange a call with our reliability lead (Victor) later this week.

Best,
Ellen
VP, Platform Engineering
StormTech

Attachment: StormTech_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 92KB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Bespoke uptime & latency commitment

Team — forwarding StormTech's ask. High-level: they want 99.95% monthly uptime + P95 <120ms for primary route, tied to a committed multi-year deal (deal ST-7821). They attached a draft SLA.

Questions for product/eng/legal before I reply to Ellen:
- Product (Aditya): Is P95 <120ms achievable on hosted with current routing/caching? If not, what changes (dedicated pool, pinned model variant, or routing policy) do we need?
- Infra/Eng (Karthik): If we dedicate capacity, what reserve size would meet a reasonable SLO for their expected QPS? What operational controls would you need (autoscale carveouts, burst lanes)?
- Contracts (Laura): What is our threshold for offering a custom uptime SLA + credits? Are there standard templates we can lean on or is this a legal redline?
- Sales (Marissa): What's their expected committed spend (ballpark) and timeline to sign?

Can each of you reply with a brief feasibility note by EOD Wednesday so I can get back to StormTech with a proposed path and timeline.

Thanks — Naomi
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Bespoke uptime & latency commitment

Short answers from product perspective:

- P95 <120ms is plausible for their inference path if we control the serving surface: dedicate the model variant (8-bit quant) + reserved GPU pool in a region close to their traffic. With current hosted routing and public multi-tenant pools, we'd see more variance and can't guarantee 120ms.

- Requirements:
  * Dedicated capacity (reserved) sized for their baseline QPS with a 2x buffer for bursts.
  * Pinning to a verified model/quantization profile we already support (we should avoid experimental kernels).
  * SLO measurement point: we should define the client-facing path (edge -> model) and exact measurement method (synthetic vs real traffic sampling).
  * Operational runbook: auto-fallback to compatible lower-cost model variant and cross-region failover as part of the rollback policy.

- Risk notes: tight P95 targets are sensitive to cold starts and noisy neighbors; dedicated capacity mitigates noisy neighbors but not hardware faults — recommend a 30-minute SLA credit window and a clear maintenance blackout policy.

I'll sync with Karthik on required infra changes; happy to draft a product-side SLO proposal for Naomi to share.

— Aditya
Director, Product Management
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Bespoke uptime & latency commitment

Thanks for the rapid responses. From a contracts/legal standpoint:

- We can support a bespoke SLA for Strategic accounts provided Procurement signs a reserved-capacity contract with a minimum commitment term (recommend 12 months) and explicit operational constraints (maintenance windows, allowed non-covered events).
- Credits: standard practice is pro-rata service credits capped (e.g., up to X% of monthly invoice) tied to clearly defined measurement windows. Laura suggests drafting a schedule with a tiered credit table for p95 and uptime breaches.
- Required items before legal sign-off:
  1) Exact SLO definitions and measurement methodology (product to provide)
  2) Capacity sizing and runbook (Karthik/product to provide)
  3) Proposed contract term and spend commitment (Marissa to confirm)

I'm OK to green-light a conditional exception if the above are provided and sales confirms committed spend >= $600k ARR equivalent. Naomi — once Aditya and Karthik share the SLO + capacity numbers, I'll prepare a redline-friendly SLA schedule for the contract team.

— Laura
Head of Contracts & Compliance
